---
title: "Exercise 3.2"
---

## Solution

Let $\{B_i\}$ be a pairwise disjoint sequence of sets in $\mathcal A$ and define
$$  A_i = \bigcup_{k=i+1}^{\infty} B_k.$$

Then $\{A_i\}$ is a decreasing sequence of sets in $\mathcal A$ and
$$ A_i \downarrow \emptyset. $$
Thus, by assumption,
$$ \mu(A_i) \to 0.$$
Since $\mu$ is finitely additive, for every $n \in \mathbb N$, we have
$$\mu \left( \bigcup B_i \right) = \mu \left(\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^{n} B_i \right)\cup A_n \right) = \mu(A_n) + \sum_{i=1}^n \mu(B_i).$$

Therefore,
$$ \sum_{i=1}^{\infty} \mu(B_i) = \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{i=1}^n \mu(B_i) = \mu \left( \bigcup B_i \right) - \lim_{n \to \infty} \mu(A_n)= \mu \left( \bigcup B_i \right).$$


Hence $\mu$ is countably additive, and therefore a measure.
